extracted.intended_audience: Authors and LaTeX users preparing mathematical documents with AMS-LaTeX (amstex, amsart, amsbook), especially for AMS publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing high-quality mathematical documents using the AMS-LaTeX amstex option and the amsart/amsbook documentstyles, covering semantic math commands, environments, spacing, numbering, and publisher conventions. Aimed at authors formatting math papers and books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dots: use semantic dot commands
rubrics_metrics.description: In the amstex option dots should be typed as \dots; placement (on the baseline or centered) is selected according to whatever follows after the \dots. When the following token gives no placement information (e.g., end of formula), use \dotsc, \dotsb, \dotsm, or \dotsi to specify meaning rather than appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \dotsc for 'dots with commas' (series A1, A2, \dotsc), \dotsb for 'dots with binary operators/relations' (A1 + A2 + \dotsb), \dotsm for 'multiplication dots' (A1A2\dotsm), and \dotsi for 'dots with integrals'. This semantic approach preserves portability across conventions; \ldots and \cdots remain available for compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accents in math: use amstex accent commands
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides capitalized accent commands (\Hat, \Breve, \Bar, \Vec, \Check, \Tilde, \Acute, \Grave, \Dot, \Ddot) that automatically position double accents properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ordinary LaTeX double accents (e.g., \hat{\hat A}) can be askew; with amstex typing \Hat{\Hat A} positions the second accent correctly. For documents with many double accents, define cached versions via \accentedsymbol to store results in a box register to speed processing (example: \accentedsymbol{\Ahathat}{\Hat{\Hat A}}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide accents and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Wide accents like \widehat and \widetilde exist but have a maximum size and may not suit extremely long expressions; alternative notations may be preferable for very long expressions or for putting accents on superscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For putting accents into superscripts, use provided sp* control sequences (e.g., \sphat, \spddot, \spcheck, \spdddot, \sptilde, \spbreve, \spdot) to simplify input. Triple and quadruple dot accents are available via \dddot and \ddddot in addition to \dot and \ddot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root index positioning with \leftroot and \uproot
rubrics_metrics.description: In amstex \leftroot and \uproot allow adjustment of the placement of root indices (e.g., \sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{2}\beta]{k} moves the index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The negative argument to \leftroot moves the index to the right; units are small dimensions appropriate for fine adjustments. See sample file for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxed formulas with \boxed
rubrics_metrics.description: The command \boxed puts a box around its argument, similar to \fbox but with the contents in math mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensible arrows with @>>> and @<<<
rubrics_metrics.description: The constructs @>>> and @<<< produce arrows that extend automatically to accommodate wide subscripts or superscripts; superscript text goes between the first and second > or <, subscript between second and third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensible arrows were developed for commutative diagrams; the amscd option must be loaded for them to function. Example: @>\xi F_k\Gamma_k\alpha>> produces a superscript placed above the arrow. See section on commutative diagrams for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \overset and \underset for general placement
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides \overset and \underset to place one symbol above or below another (more general than \stackrel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \overset{*}{X} places a superscript-size * above X; \underset performs the parallel operation for placement underneath. Use these on relations or other symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \sideset for corner symbols on large operators
rubrics_metrics.description: \sideset can put symbols at subscript and superscript corners of a large operator (e.g., sums, products), allowing primes or other symbols at corners while preserving limits behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax requires an extra pair of empty braces when appropriate (e.g., \sideset{}{'}\sum_{...} to add a prime to a sum symbol). \sideset supports putting separate symbols at each corner, e.g., \sideset{_*^*}{_*^*}\prod.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \text for words or phrases in math displays
rubrics_metrics.description: The \text command is intended for inserting words or phrases in displayed math; it acts like \mbox but is easier for subscripts and has a more descriptive name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ..._{\text{word or phrase}} is easier than ..._{\mbox{\scriptsize word or phrase}}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator names: use \operatorname and \operatornamewithlimits
rubrics_metrics.description: \operatorname{xxx} produces xxx in the proper roman font with correct spacing; \operatornamewithlimits is used when subscripts should be placed underneath in display mode (like \lim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define frequent operator names in the preamble via \newcommand{\xxx}{\operatorname{xxx}} to reduce typing. amstex also predefines some operator names with limits (\varinjlim, \varprojlim, \varliminf, \varlimsup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod notation: use specialized commands for spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands \mod, \bmod, \pmod, and \pod handle the special spacing conventions of 'mod' notation; \mod omits parentheses, \pod omits 'mod' but keeps parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In amstex the spacing of \pmod will adjust in non-display mode; prefer the variant matching conventional usage for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \dfrac and \tfrac and adjustable fraction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides \dfrac and \tfrac as abbreviations for \displaystyle and \textstyle fractions, and a square-bracket option for \frac to vary the thickness of the fraction line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: \frac[<dimension>]{...}{...} sets the horizontal rule thickness. Use \fracwithdelims to specify delimiters with better spacing than manual \left(\frac{...}{...}\right); binomial forms \binom, \dbinom, \tbinom and \binom as an abbreviation for \fracwithdelims()[0pt] are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued fractions: use \cfrac with \lcfrac/\rcfrac for placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The continued fraction construction can be built using \cfrac, with \lcfrac and \rcfrac to control left/right placement of numerators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example nested \cfrac structure shown; use \lcfrac or \rcfrac to adjust numerator placement in long continued fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smash options: use optional [t] and [b] arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex extends \smash with optional arguments t and b to smash only the top or only the bottom of something while retaining the natural depth or height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \smash[b]{...} smashes only the part extending below the baseline, useful for fine positional adjustments of subformulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use amstex cases environment for piecewise definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides a cases environment for typesetting common piecewise constructions, allowing embedded text via \text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \begin{cases} ... & \text{if ...},\\ 0 & \text{if ...} \end{cases}. Use \text inside the cases to mix text and math properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix environments and MaxMatrixCols
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex retains matrix environments (pmatrix, bmatrix, vmatrix, Vmatrix, matrix) as LaTeX environments with default formatting (up to 10 centered columns). The maximum number of columns is determined by MaxMatrixCols which can be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To increase columns, use \setcounter{MaxMatrixCols}{<n>} before the matrix. For small in-text matrices use smallmatrix environment. Use \hdotsfor{<n>} to produce a row of dots spanning the given number of columns and \hdotsfor[<multiplier>]{<n>} to vary spacing (multiplier default 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sb and Sp environments for multiline subscripts/superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sb and Sp environments typeset several lines as a subscript or superscript respectively and can be used anywhere ordinary subscripts/superscripts are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \sum\begin{Sb} 0\le i\le m\\ 0<j<n \end{Sb} P(i,j) produces a two-line subscript under the sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutative diagrams: use amscd or picture environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The commutative diagram commands from TeX are available in the amscd option (not included in amstex by default). For simple diagrams without diagonal arrows amscd is convenient; for complex diagrams use picture environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the CD environment commands @>>>, @<<<, @VVV, and @AAA give right, left, down, and up arrows respectively. Material between first/second and second/third > or < becomes superscript/subscript for horizontal arrows; similar 'sidescript' features exist for vertical arrows. Use \End as \operatorname{End} for labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer amstex alignment environments over eqnarray
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex provides several alignment environments (align, multline, gather, split, alignat, xalignat, xxalignat) which are preferable to eqnarray because they avoid overlapping equation numbers and provide better spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each environment (except split) has starred and unstarred forms (unstarred auto-numbering). Suppress numbering on a line with \notag or \nonumber, or provide custom tags with \tag{<label>} or literal \tag*{<text>}. See appendix for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use align for vertical alignment of multiple equations
rubrics_metrics.description: The align environment is used for two or more equations where vertical alignment is desired (usually aligning binary relations like '=').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'equation' here is any self-contained math formula intended as a subdivision of the larger display; use & to mark alignment points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gather when no alignment is desired
rubrics_metrics.description: The gather environment is for two or more displayed equations that are to be centered separately without alignment among them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use alignat/xalignat/xxalignat for multiple side-by-side align structures
rubrics_metrics.description: The alignat environment places multiple 'align' structures side-by-side; it requires one argument specifying the number of align structures. xalignat and xxalignat provide expanded spacing variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an argument n, the number of & per line is 2n-1 (one & for alignment within each structure and separators between structures). xalignat gives equal spacing between columns and margins; xxalignat gives equal spacing between columns and zero spacing at margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multline for single long equations over multiple lines
rubrics_metrics.description: The multline environment is for equations that do not fit on a single line: the first line is left-aligned, the last line right-aligned (with an indent on both sides equal to \multlinegap), and any intermediate lines centered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change \multlinegap with \setlength or \addtolength. Use when equation cannot be sensibly split with alignment points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use split for single equations split into aligned lines inside another display
rubrics_metrics.description: The split environment is for breaking a single equation into multiple aligned lines; it provides no numbering itself and is intended for use inside other displayed equation structures (equation, align, gather).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use & to mark alignment points as usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gathered/aligned/alignedat for sub-displays inside formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: The environments aligned, gathered, and alignedat are self-contained units usable inside other formulas or side-by-side; they take an optional argument for vertical positioning (default [c]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To align first line with adjacent material use \begin{gathered}[t] ... \end{gathered} etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical spacing and page breaks in amstex equation structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\[<dimension>] to get extra vertical space between lines in displayed equation environments. By default, amstex equation environments don’t allow page breaks between lines unless \displaybreak or \allowdisplaybreaks is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place \displaybreak before the \\ where the break is permitted; \displaybreak takes optional argument 0–4 indicating desirability (0 permissible, 4 force). \allowdisplaybreaks obeys scoping rules (use grouping to limit scope). Within an \allowdisplaybreaks scope, use \\* to prohibit a pagebreak at a particular line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \intertext for short interjections within alignments
rubrics_metrics.description: \intertext inserts a short piece of text in the middle of a display alignment while preserving alignment; it must appear immediately after a \\ or \\*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for explanatory lines between aligned equations without breaking alignment context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control equation numbering with \numberwithin and \eqref
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \numberwithin{<counter>}{<parent>} to tie a counter to another (e.g., \numberwithin{equation}{section}) so numbering resets automatically. Use \eqref{label} to produce a parenthesized equation reference with proper corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply \numberwithin cautiously to other counters because of potential complications; use normal LaTeX methods where available (e.g., \newtheorem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose 'Runaway argument?' and paragraph ended errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Runaway argument?' or 'Paragraph ended before \multline* was complete' errors usually indicate a mismatched environment (begin/end mismatch) or a missing } or \right delimiter inside an environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common cause: a missing } (easy to forget with \frac, etc.) or mismatched begin/end of an alignment environment such as \begin{multline*} ... \end{multline}. Recovery prompts in TeX may suggest commands; inspect braces and matching environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ~, \/, and \slash to manage spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: In amstex the tilde (~), \/, and \slash remove superfluous spaces on either side (\/, only the space on the left is removed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: insert ~ in 'p.~63' without deleting the existing space; use these to fine-tune interword spacing in specific contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big delimiters adjust properly over font sizes in amstex
rubrics_metrics.description: In ordinary LaTeX \big, \bigg, \Big, and \Bigg delimiters don’t adjust over the full range of LaTeX font sizes; in the amstex option they do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentstyle options controlling limits and tags
rubrics_metrics.description: amstex/AMS styles supply documentstyle options (nosumlim, intlim, nonamelm, ctagsplt, righttag) to control positioning of limits and tags and the behavior of generated names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some component packages can be loaded individually in \documentstyle options (amstext, amsbsy, amsfonts, msam, msbm, eufm, etc.). See package descriptions for provided symbols and font setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: amssymb option defines AMS symbol names
rubrics_metrics.description: The amssymb option defines names for all symbols in the AMS math symbol fonts (requires AMSFonts package, version 2.0 recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comment environment from verbatim for ignored blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: The new verbatim style option provides a comment environment: anything between \begin{comment} and \end{comment} is totally ignored by LaTeX; \end{comment} must be on its own line and comment environments cannot be nested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text after \end{comment} on the same line is ignored and generates a warning. See verbatim.doc for additional features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use syntonly option for syntax-only checking
rubrics_metrics.description: The syntonly style option allows running LaTeX with \syntaxonly in the preamble to perform syntax checking only (no output), which speeds processing and reveals LaTeX errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical speedups are 30%–40% depending on system; useful for debugging large documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect fragile commands in moving arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Many commands added by amstex are fragile and need to be \protected when used in moving arguments (e.g., \section, \caption, \addcontentsline, \addtocontents, \markboth, \markright, @-expressions in arrays/tables, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to LaTeX manual Section C.1.3 for full list and usage of \protect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special note on @ character and other LaTeX differences
rubrics_metrics.description:
In amstex the @ character has special uses (extensible arrows, math microspacing commands). To print an ordinary @ type @@. The eqnarray environment is no longer needed given amstex alignment environments. 
onumber is interchangeable with 
otag (
otag slightly preferred for consistency with 	ag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In math avoid text font commands \bf, \rm for single variables; use \bold, \mathrm, etc. instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top matter commands in amsart/amsbook and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: amsart provides an expanded top matter with commands: \keywords, \subjclass, \title, \author, \address, \translator, \dedicatory, \email, \date, \thanks. All should precede \maketitle; if abstract environment is used it should follow immediately after \maketitle. Address/email/translator info prints at document end; keywords, subject class, and thanks print as first-page footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an \author command for each author; put author-specific \address, \email, \thanks immediately after the corresponding \author and before any other \author. Double @ in e-mail addresses so they print correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory conservation: top matter commands are undeclared after use
rubrics_metrics.description: To conserve memory, commands needed only at the beginning of a document (top matter and the abstract environment) are undefined after they are no longer needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that once used and processed they may be undefined later in the run; structure preamble accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads: provide short forms with optional arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Running heads in amsart contain the article title on odd pages and the author's name on even pages; if the title or author is too long, provide a short version using the square-bracket optional argument to \title or \author (e.g., \title[Short]{Long}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English automatic text: redefine names via \renewcommand
rubrics_metrics.description: To customize automatically generated labels (e.g., 'Abstract', 'Figure', 'Table', 'Proof', 'References', etc.) for non-English documents, redefine the corresponding command names like \abstractname, \partname, \indexname, \figurename, \tablename, \proofname, \refname, \appendixname, \tocname.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits substitution of localized labels (e.g., \renewcommand{\abstractname}{R\'esum\'e}). amsbook supplies additional names (\chaptername, \listfigurename, \listtablename, \bibname).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem styles: group \newtheorem under \theoremstyle
rubrics_metrics.description: amsart/amsbook supply three \theoremstyles (plain, definition, remark) to give visual emphasis appropriate to the theorem-type; divide \newtheorem commands into groups prefaced by the desired \theoremstyle. If no \theoremstyle is given, plain is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given for common environments (thm, lem, cor, prop, defn, conj, exmp, prob, rem, note, claim, summ, case, ack). To create an unnumbered environment, \renewcommand{\the<env>}{} where <env> is the environment name; create a specifically named unnumbered theorem via a separate \newtheorem and then \renewcommand{\the...}{}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof environments and Q.E.D. symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: A predefinded pf environment and starred pf* are provided for proofs; they produce the heading 'Proof' and automatically append a Q.E.D. symbol (\qedsymbol) at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To substitute a different end-of-proof symbol, redefine \qedsymbol. The pf environment is intended for short proofs (<1 page); for longer proofs use a separate section/subsection and use \qed to produce the symbol and spacing. The starred pf* form takes an argument to change the heading (e.g., \begin{pf*}{Proof (sufficiency)}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Starred sectioning forms produce TOC entries
rubrics_metrics.description: In amsart and amsbook the starred forms of \chapter and \section produce a table of contents entry (variation from standard LaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns with usual publishing practice; be aware of differences from standard LaTeX behavior (see LaTeX manual C.3.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author names and addresses input conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: amsart/amsbook prefer separate \author and \address commands for each author rather than the standard combined \author{...\and...} format; addresses and similar elements are associated with the nearest preceding \author command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard LaTeX format will still print but addresses may not appear in the correct place (amsart prints them at the end). For AMS submissions provide at minimum title, author, addresses, subject classification numbers, translator (if applicable), and acknowledgments of funding support (\thanks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and punctuation in italic text: use \rom
rubrics_metrics.description: In mathematical publishing numbers and punctuation are set upright even inside italic text; amsart/amsbook attempt automatic fixes and provide \rom{<char>} for manual corrections to make individual punctuation marks or numbers nonitalic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '... formal \rom{(} in the previous year, \rom{1989)} ...' \rom inserts italic corrections automatically. Use \rom only for punctuation or numbers that produce noticeable slant; commas and periods often do not require it. \ref has been changed to avoid printing its numbers in italic.

rubrics_metrics.name: amsbook front-matter conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: amsbook produces a simple title page with title and author; subject class numbers, abstract, or keywords, if supplied, print on the following page. For AMS submissions provide title, author, addresses, subject classification numbers, translator (if applicable), and acknowledgments (\thanks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amsbook is intended to make it convenient for authors to provide necessary information to a publisher rather than for final publication formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: BibTeX bibliography styles amsplain and amsalpha
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS-LaTeX distribution includes two BibTeX styles amsplain and amsalpha, analogous to LaTeX's plain and alpha styles; an extra field 'language' is provided to indicate original language of a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'language' field to signal translated titles/authors so readers know to locate the original; this can assist library searches.
